Title: Iran strikes two tankers attempting Hormuz transit under US escort
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday that they had struck two tankers attempting to pass though the strategic Strait of Hormuz under the "air escort" of the US military.
The IRGC said the "non-compliant oil tankers... were struck and brought to a halt, while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions."
The Guards said the tankers had attempted to pass the strait via "an undeclared route", the US-backed alternative to Teheran's designated waterway closer to its own shores.
Iran has effectively maintained control over navigation through Hormuz since the outbreak of the war on Feb 28, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.
On Thursday, the Guards said two oil tankers attempting to transit the Strait had turned back after one caught fire.--AFP

Title: Four bodies recovered after Pakistan avalanche traps Nirmal Purja expedition
Article:
SKARDU, Pakistan: Search teams found four bodies near the site of an avalanche in northern Pakistan that left 10 people missing from a climbing expedition led by renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja, police said on Friday.
A spokesperson for police in the mountainous Gilgit-Baltistan region said search-and-rescue teams had reached the location the avalanche had struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition that had been in the area.
"Preliminary reports indicate that four (04) bodies have so far been recovered," Gilgit-Baltistan region's police spokesperson said in a statement on Facebook, adding that the condition of the remaining climbers was still being verified.
The Alpine Club of Pakistan said the expedition comprised 10 people – including five Nepalese, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, and a climber from China. Police did not mention an American citizen and said two British nationals – a man and a woman – were in the missing team.
"The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range," the club said late on Thursday.
"The entire team has reportedly been out of communication since the avalanche," it said.
Purja, 43, who served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.
He climbed all 14 "eight-thousanders" (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 – then a record.
In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 along with a team of nine other Nepali climbers.
- 'ASK FOR NOTHING' -
China's foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said they were "urgently working to verify and understand the situation" and said Beijing was willing to provide assistance to Pakistan.
Rescuers equipped with geolocation devices have been sent to search for the missing climbers, the Alpine Club said.
"Through Global Positioning System (GPS), we have already traced the locations of four climbers," Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of the Alpine Club, told AFP in the mountainous northern city of Skardu.
"For now, we can't say anything about what exactly has happened," he said.
Military helicopters were reinforcing efforts on the ground to find the climbers and boost the operation in the challenging high-altitude environment, according to the club.
Purja had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without oxygen.
"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.
"I take zero mountains for granted. Not one. The moment my foot leaves basecamp, it's 100pct. Always has been. Always will be.
"My purpose has never been about me. It's about what I represent. It's about showing YOU that your own mountains – whatever they are – are climbable."
Broad Peak is the world's 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000 metre-plus ascents.
It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.--AFP

Title: SME's strong 2025 performance reflects resilience amid global uncertainties – Samenta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The positive performance of Malaysian small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in 2025 demonstrated the incredible resilience and agility of businesses despite persistent global supply chain disruptions and shifting trade dynamics.
The Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) national president Datuk William Ng said the local SMEs have continued to invest, innovate and expand their reach into regional and international markets, and as a result, SME exports surged 10.5 per cent to RM214.5 billion.
"To sustain this momentum and reach our national target of a 40 per cent gross domestic product (GDP) contribution, we must ensure that unnecessary regulatory hurdles do not bog down our SMEs.
"While we cannot control external factors such as energy costs and geopolitics, the government can and must double down on regulatory reform to reduce compliance costs," he said in a statement.
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), MSMEs achieved a 5.7 per cent GDP growth in 2025, outpacing the broader national economy's 5.2 per cent growth over the same period.
Ng said that with value-added output reaching RM689.8 billion and contributing 39.7 per cent to Malaysia's total GDP, these figures confirm once again that SMEs are the undisputed engine of the country's economic growth.
Nearly one out of two working Malaysians are now employed by an SME, with labour productivity per employee rising 4.1 per cent to RM85,299, reflecting real, ongoing efforts by SMEs to adopt digitalisation, automation and AI tools, he said.
Meanwhile, Ng suggested that the government should focus on policies to shift from blanket grants to productivity linked incentives, particularly supporting AI adoption, digital integration and automation to offset rising labour costs.
"Furthermore, the nationwide roll-out of initiatives such as Akta Iltizam, Bureaucratic Red-tape Reform and Good Regulatory Practice must be accelerated. Ultimately, the public sector must view the private sector as equal partners in nation building," he added.
Samenta remains committed to working with the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives, Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry and various government agencies to build stronger capability for SMEs and scale sustainably into regional champions.

Title: Hamas: Israel must honour Gaza deal before disarmament
Article:
CAIRO: Implementation of the deal to bring peace to Gaza announced by US President Donald Trump will depend on Israel first meeting its commitments under an agreement reached last year, a senior Hamas official told Reuters on Friday.
In a post on his Truth Social platform on Thursday, Trump announced a "major milestone" towards ending the war in Gaza, saying his "Board of Peace" had reached an agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups.
Ghazi Hamad, a Hamas official involved in the negotiations, said the agreement was a "comprehensive framework" that went beyond the issue of disarmament and would depend on Israel implementing the first phase of an agreement hammered out last year in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.
Under that agreement, he said Israel was obliged to end its attacks in Gaza and withdraw its forces to where they stood in October, as well as increase the flow of goods and aid coming into the enclave.
Only then would Hamas agree to hand over its weapons to the new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), the technocratic body set up to run the enclave.
"We insisted to the mediators that Israel must abide by the agreement," he said. On Thursday, an Israeli official said Israel would not agree to withdraw behind the so-called Yellow Line before Hamas is disarmed and the Gaza Strip is demilitarised.--REUTERS

Title: Ringgit ends week marginally higher against US dollar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended the week marginally higher against the US dollar following weaker-than-expected US economic data although sentiment towards the greenback remained firm, as expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike in September stayed intact.
At 6pm, the local currency appreciated to 4.0835/0875 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0875/0930.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said expectations of a September interest rate hike by the Fed stayed intact despite weaker US economic data, helping to limit the US dollar's losses.
"The United States' second-quarter 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth came in below expectations at 1.5 per cent compared with the consensus estimate of 2.1 per cent.
"Meanwhile, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, moderated to 3.7 per cent in June from 4.1 per cent in May," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies at the close.
It eased versus the Japanese yen to 2.5520/5548 from 2.5029/5064 at Thursday's close, depreciated vis-à-vis the euro to 4.6981/7027 from 4.6863/6926 yesterday and declined versus the British pound to 5.4923/4977 from 5.4691/4764 previously.
The ringgit also traded lower against regional currencies.
It weakened versus the Thai baht to 12.2264/2435 from 12.1637/1852 at yesterday's close, declined against the Indonesian rupiah to 226.6/226.8 from 225.7/226.0 previously, depreciated vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.66/6.67 from 6.64/6.65, and slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.1823/1856 from 3.1701/1746.

Title: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump Gaza plan, Israel yet to respond
Article:
GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Hamas said Friday it had agreed to a deal announced by US President Donald Trump to end the war with Israel, that includes it handing over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza.
Israel did not immediately comment on the announcement, but shortly beforehand an Israeli political source had told AFP the proposed agreement did not "satisfactorily" address Israeli demands for the full demilitarisation of the Gaza Strip.
The source also said that "the issue of Gaza did not come up at all" in this week's meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Trump in Washington.
The group's weapons have been one of the key sticking points in implementing a ceasefire deal in place since October, but Trump announced late Thursday an agreement for Hamas's "complete disarmament", calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza.
Hamas officials told AFP that a committee established by Trump's Board of Peace to govern Gaza would oversee the process of storing the movement's weapons.
The group said it expected mediators and the Board of Peace to ensure Israel complied with the deal's terms, which include Israel's withdrawal from Gaza.
Ghazi Hamad, a member of the group's negotiating team, said the movement was making "concessions for the sake of our people in the Gaza Strip, to save them from killing and displacement."
"Israel will not intervene in the issue of disarmament. The National Committee is the body that will undertake this task," he said, referring to the National Committee for Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Despite the October ceasefire, violence has continued in Gaza, with Israeli strikes killing at least four people, including two children, on Thursday, according to health officials.
- FOCUS NOW ON IMPLEMENTATION -
The Board of Peace confirmed in a post on X that Hamas had "agreed to a detailed Roadmap for implementing the next phases of the Gaza ceasefire."
"Our focus now turns to implementation," the organisation wrote, adding the NCAG will "soon begin a phased transition toward full authority."
Trump, in an earlier social media post, said that once Hamas is disarmed "Israeli forces will withdraw, and the International Stabilisation Force will work with a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza being safe for its residents and its neighbours."
Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, said Friday the deal "took months of very difficult negotiations."
"What happens next matters even more. Implementation and verification have to be real," Mladenov wrote on X.
"Withdrawal must move in lockstep with decommissioning," he added.
- 'NO EXCEPTIONS' -
Egypt's state-linked Al-Qahera News said Friday that Cairo will soon host a meeting soon of the truce mediators, which also include the United States, Qatar and Turkiye, focused on the second phase of the ceasefire plan.
Earlier, a diplomatic source told AFP: "We continue to advance the implementation roadmap that offers a balanced and pragmatic path forward, with all weapons decommissioned and a phased transition of responsibilities taking place to hand over full authority to the technocratic government."
The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity as he was not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, said there would be "no exceptions for certain weapons or certain people. One authority, one law, one weapon."
The roadmap, the source said, would create "a process for the elimination of all tunnels, depots of weapons and any weapons production facilities."
The source said a verification mechanism would ensure compliance by each side.
A Hamas source familiar with the talks told AFP earlier that the movement was "awaiting the Israeli response to the amendments we recently submitted to the mediators."
The source said the amendments concerned two articles in the roadmap presented by the Board of Peace.
Regarding the article concerning weapons, the Hamas source said that "some points were removed, and alternatives were proposed."
Before the deal's announcement, the Israeli political source told AFP: "Israel demands the complete disarmament of Hamas, including the removal of weapons from Gaza and full demilitarisation of the Strip as a precondition for any process." --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher on blue-chip buying, tracks most regional markets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher on Friday as investors continued to accumulate blue-chip stocks in line with stronger performances across most regional markets.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 4.50 points to 1,724.90 from yesterday's close of 1,720.40.
The benchmark index opened 0.83 of a point higher at 1,721.23, and moved between 1,715.67 and 1,730.12 throughout the day.
The broader market was positive with gainers outpacing losers 707 to 402, while 547 counters were unchanged, 1,085 untraded and 56 suspended.
Turnover expanded to 3.03 billion units valued at RM3.56 billion from 2.49 billion units valued at RM2.25 billion on Thursday.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng noted that across the region, most major indices closed in positive territory with strong gains in South Korea, while the Bank of Japan's decision to leave interest rates unchanged was largely in line with market expectations.
Regionally, South Korea's KOSPI Composite Index surged 17.91 per cent to 6,595.45, Japan's Nikkei 225 soared 4.03 per cent to 64,362.02, and Shanghai's SSE Composite Index improved 0.72 per cent to 3,832.26, Indonesia's IDX Composite Index inched up 0.80 per cent to 6,236.13, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index gained 0.10 per cent to 25,884.43.
Meanwhile, Singapore's Straits Times Index declined 0.79 per cent to 5,628.50.
On the domestic front, Thong said sentiment has improved following the return of foreign buying, providing additional support to the local market.
"Blue chips have the strongest fundamentals and high turnaround for the past two days," he told Bernama.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank added two sen to RM10.90, Public Bank perked up one sen to RM5.17, CIMB added six sen to RM7.89, IHH Healthcare was unchanged to RM8.35, while Tenaga Nasional fell two sen to RM14.60.
As for the active stocks, Zetrix AI put on three sen to 74.5 sen, Nationgate climbed six sen to RM1.19, V.S Industry edged up one sen each to 23 sen, TWL inched up half-a-sen to 2.5 sen, and Inari Amertron increased 10 sen to RM2.22.
Of the lead gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries garnered RM3.00 to RM46.00, Nestlé gained RM1.60 to RM101.10, ViTrox jumped 70 sen to RM8.70, UMS Integration leapt 51 sen to RM7.35, and Petronas Dagangan advanced 32 sen to RM19.52.
Hong Leong Industries led the losers list, falling 28 sen to RM17.72, Allianz Malaysia lost 20 sen to RM21.00, Kuala Lumpur Kepong eased 18 sen to RM21.02, Concrete Engineering Products slid 14 sen to RM3.32, and MISC fell 13 sen to RM7.99.

Title: CAAM probing if there were security lapses before pilot's departure to Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) is investigating whether there were any regulatory or security lapses which led to a Malaysian pilot departing Malaysia, and later being detained in Indonesia, over alleged drug smuggling.
CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said they are aware of the reported incident involving the Malaysian pilot and was currently gathering the relevant facts.
"The matter will be investigated from a regulatory perspective, including the airline's compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and the airport operator's security processes, to determine whether there were any lapses prior to his departure from Malaysia," Norazman said.
He added that as an immediate measure, CAAM is strengthening its oversight of existing regulatory requirements relating to baggage screening and security procedures, including those applicable to aircraft crew.
Indonesian authorities arrested a 39-year-old Malaysian pilot at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta on Tuesday for allegedly attempting to smuggle about 25kg of MDMA (ecstasy) and a small amount of methamphetamine into the country.
He also tested positive for meth, MDMA, and cocaine after flying a passenger plane to Indonesia.
Malaysia's federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect will face legal action under Indonesian law.
Malaysia Airlines, meanwhile, said it was conducting an internal review after a pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: E&O to acquire prime Jalan Kia Peng site with Majestic Gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eastern & Oriental Bhd (E&O) and Majestic Gen Sdn Bhd are acquiring a prime freehold site along Jalan Kia Peng, strengthening E&O's premium development landbank in Kuala Lumpur.
The acquisition will be undertaken through KP Urban Sdn Bhd, which is 66.67 per cent owned by E&O subsidiary KCB Holdings Sdn Bhd and 33.33 per cent by Golden Urban Nite Sdn Bhd, an affiliate of Majestic Gen.
The 5,682-square metre site, located within the Jalan Kia Peng-KLCC precinct, sits opposite The RuMa Hotel & Residences and next to the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
E&O and Majestic Gen plan to develop the site into a signature high-rise residential project, combining E&O's placemaking expertise with Majestic Gen's development capabilities to create a premium residential address.
E&O managing director Kok Tuck Cheong said securing the Jalan Kia Peng site marks an important milestone in the group's growth strategy.
"Jalan Kia Peng is one of Kuala Lumpur's most established and desirable addresses, and securing this prime freehold site allows us to create another thoughtfully designed development that reflects E&O's commitment to placemaking, design excellence and enduring value.
"Building on the encouraging performance of Conlay and the continued momentum of our flagship Andaman Island development in Penang, this acquisition will further strengthen E&O's premium development portfolio across Malaysia's residential markets.
"More importantly, it reinforces our confidence in the long-term fundamentals of Kuala Lumpur's high-end residential sector and our ability to create sustainable value for our shareholders," he said in a statement.
Majestic Gen group managing director Ta Wee Dher said Jalan Kia Peng is one of the few remaining freehold addresses in Kuala Lumpur's city centre.
He said the acquisition reflects both parties' confidence in the location's long-term appeal and provides a strong foundation for a disciplined, long-term development approach.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SCIB secures RM11.9mil EPCC contract in Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has secured a RM11.9 million engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) subcontract for upgrading works at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, SCIB said the contract was awarded to its wholly owned subsidiary, SCIB Industrialised Building System Sdn Bhd (SIBS), by Demi Cerah Construction Sdn Bhd.
The project involves upgrading the air-conditioning system at the Faculty of Engineering building under Phase 1, Package 8 of the UMS development programme. Construction is scheduled to begin on Aug 1 and is expected to be completed by July 3, 2027.
SCIB non-independent non-executive chairman Datuk Chong Loong Men said the contract further strengthens the group's construction and EPCC portfolio while expanding its presence in Sabah.
"This contract represents another meaningful addition to SCIB's construction and EPCC portfolio and further strengthens our presence in Sabah, highlighting the group's continued growth in the region.
"Our engineering, procurement and construction capabilities enable us to deliver projects efficiently while maintaining high standards of quality and execution," he said.
Chong said the upgrading works require close coordination across engineering, procurement and on-site implementation, areas where SCIB has continued to strengthen its execution capabilities.
SCIB said the contract is expected to contribute positively to future earnings, with revenue and profit to be recognised progressively based on the progress of the works.
The project will be funded through a combination of internally generated funds and external financing where required.
The group said the latest contract reinforces its position in Sabah, where continued investment in education, public facilities and infrastructure is creating opportunities for qualified construction and EPCC contractors.
SCIB said it will continue to focus on securing projects that complement its core expertise, support sustainable order book growth and enhance long-term earnings visibility while strengthening its presence in East Malaysia.

Title: #NSTviral: RXZ Members 8.0: Divided views after Gambang petrol station congestion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A crowd of motorcyclists at an R&R petrol station in Gambang, Pahang, ahead of the RXZ Members 8.0 event has sparked mixed reactions online, with some users criticising the congestion while others defending the riders.
The incident, captured in a video posted by a Threads user, has since garnered more than 1.1 million views. The user claimed the
gathering disrupted motorists
and called for such events to be stopped.
Some users suggested petrol station operators allocate separate lanes for motorcycles and cars to ease congestion.
One user said the petrol station management should have provided separate pumps for cars, describing it as unfair for motorists to wait behind hundreds of motorcycles.
However, others defended the gathering, saying participants should not be judged based on negative perceptions associated with motorcycle groups.
A user said many participants were educated, working people and that the gathering was simply a shared hobby.
"Do you know some of them are educated? Some serve the community better than those making such comments. This is just their hobby," the user said.
Another user, who claimed to have been at the location, said there was no need to make a fuss as some riders had given way to motorists needing to refuel.
"Last night I wanted to refuel, but they allowed us to do so first. Respect them, there is no need to make a fuss," the user said.
Another user also cautioned against stereotyping all motorcycle enthusiasts as reckless riders, saying many participants were families and hobbyists attending the gathering.
"Not everyone who joins this event is a 'mat rempit' with no manners. Most are husbands and fathers. There are even older men attending. They are just enjoying a gathering based on a shared interest," the user said.
The RXZ Members 8.0 motorcycle gathering is being held at the Gong Badak Motor Racing Circuit in Kuala Nerus, Terengganu, over two days from today.
On July 28, Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said police would use intelligence-gathering methods and video recordings as evidence.
He said police would engage with
youths through road safety
briefings and guidance sessions but would not compromise on offences that endangered other road users.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang drug raids lead to three arrests, discovery of smoke grenades
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police crippled a drug trafficking syndicate, seizing various drugs and two smoke hand grenades during coordinated raids that led to the arrest of three suspects.
Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the first raid was carried out by the district police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department at a house in Taman Gemilang Indah here at about 6.40pm on Thursday, following intelligence on suspected drug trafficking activities.
He said a man and a woman, both aged 47, were arrested during the operation.
"A search of the house led to the seizure of suspected heroin, methamphetamine and ganja, as well as equipment believed to have been used to package and distribute the drugs.
"Police also found an iron box containing two smoke hand grenades concealed inside a kitchen cabinet," he said today.
Nik Aminuddin said, acting on further intelligence gathered during the operation, police conducted a follow-up raid and arrested another man, aged 46.
He said checks showed the first male suspect had one previous drug-related offence, while the other two suspects had no prior criminal or drug records.
"Preliminary urine screening found the first suspect tested positive for ganja, while the second and third suspects tested negative for drug abuse.
"Police also took action under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988 by seizing three cars, five motorcycles, three gold rings and RM5,700 in cash.
"The total value of the assets seized is estimated at RM303,400," he said.
He said the three suspects were remanded for seven days from July 31 until Aug 6 to facilitate investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B, Section 6 and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Section 8 of the Explosives Act 1957.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian embassy seeks consular access to pilot detained in Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTA: The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta is seeking consular access to a Malaysian pilot detained in Indonesia on alleged drug trafficking offences following his arrest at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport earlier this week.
The embassy said it had received official notification from Indonesia's Directorate of Drug Crimes under the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) regarding the detention of the Malaysian national at Terminal 3 of the airport.
"The embassy respects Indonesia's legal process and is engaging with the Indonesian authorities to obtain consular access to the Malaysian citizen concerned," the embassy said in a statement on Friday.
The statement came shortly after
Indonesian authorities
in a press conference announced that the 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was arrested on July 29 after allegedly attempting to smuggle about 25kg of ecstasy, valued at around Rp60 billion (Rp1 million = RM225.20).
Authorities said the drugs, comprising about 70,114 ecstasy pills and 4g gross of methamphetamine, were allegedly concealed in the suspect's luggage and were discovered during an inspection at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
Investigators said preliminary findings indicated the suspect may have smuggled narcotics into Indonesia on previous occasions and is believed to be part of an international drug trafficking network, with investigations continuing to identify other members of the syndicate and the intended recipients of the drugs in the republic.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wife of missing pastor appeals to Anwar over probe stay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of missing Pastor Raymond Koh has appealed directly to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to intervene after the Court of Appeal stayed a High Court order requiring police to recommence investigations into her husband's 2017 disappearance.
In a heartfelt letter, Susanna Liew said she was appealing to Anwar because time was of the essence in the investigation into her husband's disappearance.
"I write not as a litigant, but as a wife who has been left in unbearable uncertainty. I do not know where my husband is. I do not know if he is safe. I do not know if I will ever see him again," she said.
Liew also questioned why the investigative portion of the High Court's order had been stayed, saying it was never intended to determine guilt or impose findings against any person.
"It is simply to ensure that the circumstances surrounding the disappearance were properly, diligently and independently investigated.
"I have always believed that the judiciary would remain the final sanctuary for truth and justice, the last bastion available to a family seeking answers when all other avenues have failed.
"I therefore held the sincere hope that any injustice arising from the stay of the order would be promptly corrected by the Court of Appeal."
Liew is seeking immediate intervention after the Court of Appeal on July 29 dismissed her application to lift the stay on investigations ordered by the High Court.
She said the stay, granted on Jan 26 this year, had effectively halted the investigative steps ordered by the High Court and "brought to a standstill the very investigative processes" intended to locate her husband.
The Court of Appeal maintained the stay when it dismissed her application on July 29.
Susanna said she was "shocked and troubled" by the decision, stressing that time was of the essence.
"What has caused me the greatest pain is that the stay was sought by parties who were themselves involved in the earlier investigative process, yet the consequence of that stay is that the renewed investigation ordered by the court has been prevented from taking place.
"The passage of time has caused immeasurable anxiety and distress.
"Every day that the investigations remain halted is another day in which the truth becomes more difficult to uncover, evidence becomes more vulnerable and the possibility of obtaining justice for my husband diminishes."
She added that the prejudice suffered was not merely legal but deeply personal, profound and irreparable.
"No future order of any court can ever restore what is lost in time. The damage caused is permanent, striking at the very heart of any hope for a fair and meaningful search for answers and my quest for justice."
Liew reminded Anwar that investigations by the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) in 2019 and a cabinet-appointed Special Task Force (STF) in 2020 had both concluded that state agents were involved and had recommended urgent, independent and comprehensive investigations.
She said those findings, together with the High Court's clear and unequivocal judgment based on the evidence, underscored the need for investigations to resume without delay.
Koh was abducted by a group of armed men while driving along Jalan SS4B/10 in Petaling Jaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unisem Q2 net profit rises 8.5pct on stronger sales volumes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Unisem (M) Bhd's net profit rose 8.5 per cent to RM9.91 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM9.13 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 20 per cent to RM570.12 million from RM475.15 million.
The semiconductor packaging and testing group said the stronger revenue was driven by higher sales volumes across its key operating units, although earnings growth was partly offset by higher operating expenses.
For the first half of the financial year, however, Unisem slipped into a net loss of RM3.45 million from a net profit of RM15.14 million a year earlier despite recording higher revenue.
The group attributed the loss to foreign exchange movements and higher operating expenses.
First-half revenue rose 14.6 per cent to RM1.03 billion from RM898.77 million in the corresponding period last year.
Looking ahead, Unisem remains optimistic about its prospects, supported by ongoing efficiency improvements and cost mitigation initiatives despite cost inflation and currency volatility arising from a weaker US dollar.
The group said customer demand continues to improve, driven by ongoing new product qualifications, production ramp-up activities and healthy order momentum.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Papagomo acquittal set aside, High Court orders defence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today ordered blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris to enter his defence on a charge of making seditious remarks by alleging that the current government was pro-Israel.
Judge Nurulhuda Nur'Aini Mohamad Nor allowed the prosecution's appeal and overturned the Sessions Court's earlier decision to acquit Wan Azri.
In her ruling, Nurulhuda held that the prosecution had successfully established a prima facie case under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act.
She ordered Wan Azri to enter his defence before the same Sessions Court judge, Siti Aminah Ghazali.
The court granted Wan Azri RM7,000 bail with one surety and fixed Aug 11 for mention.
After the proceedings, lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali said the defence had already presented its case during the prosecution stage and would reiterate those arguments when Wan Azri enters his defence.
The prosecution was represented by deputy public prosecutors Mohamad Mustaffa P Kunyalam, Deepa Nair Thevaharan and Nadia Mohd Izhar.
On Sept 3 last year, Siti Aminah freed
Wan Azri
at the end of the prosecution's case, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case warranting him to enter his defence.
In the appeal, Mustaffa argued that the charge was valid and not defective.
He submitted that the prosecution had established a prima facie case against Wan Azri, as the respondent, in accordance with Section 173(f)(i) of the Criminal Procedure Code.
He said the prosecution had established that the respondent uttered the seditious words, as testified by the first prosecution witness, Hisham Sharudin, who viewed a video containing statements of a seditious nature made by a person he identified as Wan Azri.
He submitted that the words used by the respondent in delivering the speech had a tendency to incite hatred and arouse feelings of disaffection against the government, amounting to a seditious tendency.
Mustaffa also argued that the withdrawal of the police report by Hisham should not be given undue weight in determining whether the prosecution had proven its case.
Rafique argued that the prosecution's case was significantly weakened following the withdrawal of the police report.
He maintained that the Sessions Court had reached the correct decision based on the evidence and applicable laws, and that there was no basis for the High Court to intervene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian artiste fined RM500 for airport outburst, pleads guilty to drug charge
Article:
SEPANG: Indonesian actor and model Samudera Hurley Taylor was fined RM500 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of using insulting words against airline staff members and disobeying orders from authorities at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani imposed the fines on the 24-year-old and ordered him to serve one month in jail for each charge if he failed to pay them.
The charges were read out to Samudera in Bahasa Melayu after confirming that he understood the language.
On the first charge, he was fined the maximum RM400 for disobeying lawful orders issued by auxiliary police officers.
Samudera was charged with disrupting public order and flight operations by failing to comply with instructions to remain calm, refrain from causing disturbance and proceed directly to board his flight.
The offence carries a maximum fine of RM400, jail of up to one month, or both upon conviction.
For a second charge, Samudera was fined RM100 for causing public disturbance by behaving in a disorderly manner.
He was accused of shouting, using abusive and provocative language towards airline staff and auxiliary police officers, and disturbing ticket counter personnel.
The offences were committed between 7.20pm and 8.12pm on July 27 at Gate 4 of the KLIA main terminal building.
Lawyer Shah Wira Abdul Halim asked the court to impose fines on his client, who was transiting from Cambodia en route to Jakarta, Indonesia, when the incident occurred.
"He has pleaded guilty and apologised to the court, police and airline staff for his unruly behaviour.
"He used inappropriate words because he was intoxicated, could not control his emotions and was barred from boarding the plane.
"He has no prior convictions in Malaysia. He is not a hardened criminal, and I ask for a rehabilitative sentence," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Farah Nabihah Sofian urged the court to consider the impact of Samudera's actions, which caused a commotion at the airport and affected airline staff members and tourists.
"For the sake of public interest, I ask the court to impose a proportionate sentence as a reminder to other tourists to observe proper etiquette when travelling in Malaysia," she said.
Separately, Samudera also pleaded guilty to self-administering the drug 11-nor-delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol-9-carboxylic acid. The offence was allegedly committed at 5.40pm at the KLIA Airport Management Centre toilet on July 28.
The charge carries a maximum RM5,000 fine or a jail term not exceeding two years upon conviction.
Farah Nabihah did not offer bail pending a pathology report. However, Shah Wira urged the court to impose a minimal bail for his client pending the submission of the report.
"The results may take some time, and I ask that the process be expedited. My client has no intention of remaining here as he wishes to return to his home country.
"If bail is granted, my client, through his representative, will provide two local sureties while the court retains his passport," he said.
Khairatul allowed bail of RM3,000 with two local sureties. She also ordered Samudera to surrender his passport and report to the police station once a month.
The court fixed Sept 9 for mention. After the proceedings, Samudera's bailors posted bail, and the fines for the airport offences were paid.

Title: Accountability, enforcement key to curb illegal cigarette trade: Coffee shops association
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Singapore Coffee Shop Proprietors' General Association (MSCSPGA) has called for sustained enforcement against the illegal cigarette trade and greater transparency through the public release of the Health Ministry's registry of legally registered cigarette brands.
The call follows a consumer perception survey by Wawasanex, which found that 68.8 per cent of Malaysians surveyed identified the seller of illegal cigarettes as a foreign national, while 99 per cent said illegal cigarettes were easy or very easy to obtain.
MSCSPGA said the findings echo concerns recently raised at Cabinet level by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who directed strict enforcement against parties found abusing business licences and visas.
According to the association, such abuses have allowed the illegal cigarette trade to operate openly at the retail level, with foreign workers increasingly being used to sell illicit cigarettes.
"Our members operate legitimate businesses that serve communities across the country," said Wong Teu Hoon, president of MSCSPGA.
"The growing presence of illicit cigarette sales involving foreign workers not only harms legitimate retailers, but also exposes illegal practices that allow the illicit trade to thrive. These gaps must be addressed through stronger enforcement and accountability," he added.
Illegal cigarettes are estimated to sell for less than half the price of legal products, with the illicit trade costing the government an estimated RM5 billion in lost tax revenue each year.
Wong said this creates an uneven playing field for businesses that comply with the law.
He added that retailers also face difficulties distinguishing between legal and illegal products, highlighting the need for clearer access to official information.
"Coffee shop owners and small retailers are already dealing with rising rental, utilities, labour and raw material costs.
"Competing against illegal products sold openly at a fraction of the price is simply not sustainable," he said.
The survey also found that 87 per cent of respondents support stricter penalties for those involved in the illegal cigarette trade.
Wong said enforcement should target not only frontline sellers, but also those enabling the trade.
"Enforcement agencies have taken meaningful action at known hotspots, and this must continue without interruption.
"Parties found to be abusing work permits and business licences to facilitate this trade should face the full range of penalties available, including revocation of permits and licences, and shop closures," he said.
MSCSPGA urged enforcement agencies to carry out regular operations against retail outlets selling illegal cigarettes, stressing that enforcement must be continuous to prevent illegal operators from returning to the market.
"Enforcement cannot be a one-off effort. Regular and sustained action is needed to ensure illegal cigarette sellers do not continue operating openly and undermine legitimate retailers who follow the rules," said Wong.
MSCSPGA also called on the Ministry of Health to publish the registry of legally registered cigarette brands under the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 as products receive approval, instead of waiting until all applications have been processed.
"The legal requirement already exists. Making the registry publicly available would give retailers and consumers a reliable way to verify legitimate products and make it harder for illicit cigarettes to enter the market."

Title: UNHCR cardholders subject to Malaysian laws, says Immigration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Holders of valid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards are still regarded as illegal immigrants, but are exempted from prosecution under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences of overstaying and entering the country without valid travel documents, according to the Immigration Department.
Apart from these exemptions, UNHCR cardholders remain subject to Malaysian laws, the department said in a statement to Bernama today.
Immigration said the public should not take matters into their own hands against foreigners, as doing so could have implications for security, public order and the law.
"The department understands that this issue has generated various reactions and concerns among the public.
"It must be emphasised that any action involving foreigners should be left to the relevant authorities and carried out in accordance with the law," the statement said.
The Immigration Department urged those with information on any foreigners suspected of violating immigration laws to report the matter to the department or the relevant enforcement agencies so that appropriate action can be taken in accordance with the law.
A group of
113 immigrants including 110 Rohingya refugees
arrived in the federal capital early last Monday on three buses after being evicted from their settlement in Penang.
They set up tents outside the UNHCR office as a temporary shelter before being moved to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters for documentation purposes and later relocated in stages to three states with the coordination of NGOs and the UNHCR.

Title: Neighbour recalls quiet family after mother, daughters found dead
Article:
IPOH: A neighbour of a woman and her two young daughters, who were found dead at their home in Bandar Baru Tambun here last night, described them as a quiet family who kept mostly to themselves.
The neighbour, who wished to be known only as Siti, 60, said the family had lived in the area for about 10 years and were rarely seen outside their home except for routine activities.
She said she last saw the family during her child's wedding, where they attended as guests.
"They came to my child's wedding. I remember seeing the family there.
"Other than that, they rarely came out of the house. I would usually only see them leaving the house to throw out rubbish, normally on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, but we did not really have conversations," she said when met at the scene today.
Checks at the scene found a car still parked at the house's car porch, but there was no sign of the family or anyone else at the residence.
Siti said she previously saw the deceased woman's elderly father coming out of the house, but had not seen him recently.
She said that the woman was also often seen driving her children to school.
"Although I saw her around, I was not very close to the family. They were very private and kept to themselves," she said.
Earlier, it was reported that
the 46-year-old woman and her daughters,
aged 12 and 11, were found dead in a bedroom of their home.
Police also found a container believed to contain the remains of burnt charcoal in the room.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police received a report at 9.10pm.
"Initial investigations found the three victims dead in a room of the house. A container believed to contain the remains of burnt charcoal was also found," he said in a statement.

Title: Malaysia's population grows, 12 states hit ageing status
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's population is estimated to increase by 0.5 per cent to 34.4 million in 2026, up from 34.2 million in 2025.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said the citizen population is projected to rise from 30.8 million in 2025 to 31.0 million in 2026, representing a growth rate of 0.6 per cent
In contrast, the non-citizen population is expected to continue declining, with a negative growth rate of 0.5 per cent in 2025 and 0.2 per cent in 2026.
At the state level, Terengganu recorded the highest population growth rate at 1.2 per cent, surpassing the national average, followed by Kelantan (1.0 per cent), Selangor (0.6 per cent), Putrajaya (0.6 per cent) and Pahang (0.6 per cent).
"Selangor continues to record the largest share of the population in 2026 at 21.7 per cent, followed by Johor (12.3 per cent) and Sabah (11.0 per cent), while Labuan and Putrajaya recorded the smallest population shares at 0.3 per cent and 0.4 per cent respectively," DOSM said in a statement today.
DOSM said the proportion of the population aged between zero and 14 years declined from 21.6 per cent in 2025 to 21.2 per cent in 2026, while the working-age population (15 to 64 years) remained unchanged at 70.4 per cent.
During the same period, the proportion of those aged 65 and above increased from 8.0 per cent to 8.4 per cent.
Putrajaya recorded the highest proportion of young people at 31.4 per cent, while Kuala Lumpur had the highest proportion of working-age residents at 76.0 per cent.
DOSM said 12 states have now attained ageing state status, with Perak continuing to record the highest proportion of residents aged 65 and above at 10.8 per cent.
A state is classified as an ageing state when those aged 65 and above account for more than seven per cent of its total population.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's median age increased to 31.7 years in 2026 from 31.3 years in 2025.
The male population rose from 17.9 million to 18.0 million, while the female population increased from 16.3 million to 16.4 million. However, the overall sex ratio remained unchanged at 110 males for every 100 females.
Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest sex ratio, with 117 males for every 100 females, while Perlis and Putrajaya were the only two states where females outnumbered males.
DOSM also said the overall dependency ratio edged down slightly to 42.0 in 2026 from 42.1 in 2025, due to a decline in the youth dependency ratio.
However, the old-age dependency ratio increased to 11.9 from 11.4.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's population density increased to 104 people per sqkm, up from 103 people per sqkm in 2025, with Kuala Lumpur remaining the most densely populated area at 8,574 people per sqkm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ilham Centre: Malay vote consolidation gives BN-PN advantage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are poised to wrest control of Negri Sembilan with at least 22 seats in tomorrow's election, with a two-thirds majority also within reach, according to Ilham Centre.
The pollster projected Pakatan Harapan (PH) to win a minimum of nine of the 36 state seats, while five constituencies — Chennah, Linggi, Nilai, Repah and Temiang — remain too close to call.
"Overall, Ilham Centre's projection shows that BN and PN collectively have the potential to control 22 state seats and form a stable majority bloc, while PH is expected to win a minimum of nine seats," it said in a statement today.
It said if BN-PN managed to capture several of the five closely contested seats, the alliance could surpass the 24 seats needed for a two-thirds majority in the state legislative assembly.
Ilham attributed the projection largely to the consolidation of Malay support behind BN and PN, saying Malay-Muslim identity politics had emerged as the dominant factor shaping voter behaviour.
"The campaign is no longer focused solely on the government's administrative record, development or performance, but has shifted towards issues of identity such as religion, the position of the Malays and Malay political power," it said.
Ilham said cooperation between BN and PN had also translated into stronger-than-expected vote transfers between supporters of the two parties.
Its findings estimated that about 92 per cent of PN supporters would back BN candidates in BN-contested seats, while about 75 per cent of BN supporters would transfer their votes to PN candidates.
"The process of vote transfer between BN and PN supporters took place much more effectively than initially expected," it said.
It said the consolidation had placed PH at a significant disadvantage in Malay-majority constituencies, estimating that the coalition had secured only about 18 per cent of Malay voters' support.
Ilham said PH had failed to offer a counter-narrative capable of matching the emotional appeal of the identity-based campaign, despite highlighting the state government's administrative record, governance and achievements.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun, however, remained personally popular, with Ilham putting his approval rating at about 75 per cent, although the support had not translated into wider backing for PH.
"His personal popularity did not succeed in translating into wider electoral support for PH," it said, adding that Aminuddin's move from Sikamat to the more challenging Linggi seat had also forced him to concentrate much of his campaign on defending his own constituency."
Polling will begin at 8am tomorrow at 401 polling centres across the state, with 103 candidates vying for 36 seats.
Pakatan Harapan is contesting all 36 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (25), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (24), Perikatan Nasional (11), four Independents, while Berjasa, Parti Orang Asli Malaysia and Parti Sosialis Malaysia are fielding one candidate each.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri polls: Anwar confident of PH victory, focus on stability
Article:
SEREMBAN: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he is confident the coalition can secure victory in tomorrow's polls.
Asked for his forecast of PH's performance in the Negri Sembilan election, Anwar said the coalition would focus on doing its best.
"God willing, we will do our very best, and God willing, we are confident that we can secure a victory," he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Kariah Paroi Jaya today.
The prime minister said the priority was to remain focused and ensure the situation stays stable after the election through cooperation from all parties.
When asked how many seats Pakatan Harapan expects to win, Anwar declined to give a figure, saying: "You'll have to ask Aminuddin (Negri Sembilan caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun)."
Tomorrow, 859,750 of Negri Sembilan's 889,940 registered voters will head to the polls to decide who will govern the state for the next five years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RXZ gathering tragedy: Three riders killed in Pahang crashes
Article:
KUANTAN: Three motorcyclists heading to the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering in Kuala Terengganu were killed, while two others were injured in four separate crashes across Pahang within 12 hours.
The crashes occurred between 10.10pm yesterday and 10.10am today in Maran, Temerloh and Rompin, involving riders travelling to the annual motorcycle gathering.
In Maran, two riders were killed in separate crashes along the East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT1) near the Sri Jaya Toll Plaza interchange.
Maran district police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the first crash occurred at 6.30am when Mohd Fauzi Othman, 44, lost control of his motorcycle at Km184.9 of LPT1 while travelling with friends from Kuala Lumpur to Kuala Terengganu.
"The victim was riding in a convoy with friends when the motorcycle is believed to have lost control and skidded, causing him to fall onto the right lane of the expressway," he said.
The victim was pronounced dead at the scene.
About four hours later, another rider, Muhamad Fikri Jamallunasi, 34, was killed after his motorcycle crashed into the rear of a pickup truck that had stopped on the emergency lane to assist another convoy participant whose motorcycle had broken down.
Wong said the impact threw the victim onto the expressway, where he died at the scene.
Both bodies were sent to Jengka Hospital for post-mortem examinations.
In Temerloh, a 19-year-old night market trader was killed after his motorcycle skidded and collided with a car at Km112.3 of LPT1 at about 11pm yesterday.
Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said Muhammad Zulhairi Azhar Mohd Shahrizan was travelling from Kuala Lumpur towards Kuantan when he lost control of his motorcycle and fell onto the right lane.
He said a car driven by a 23-year-old woman travelling in the same direction was unable to avoid the motorcycle, resulting in the fatal collision.
Police also found that the victim did not have a valid driving licence.
His body was taken to Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital in Temerloh for a post-mortem.
The fatal crashes in Maran and Temerloh are being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Meanwhile, in Rompin, two riders were injured after two motorcycles caught fire following a collision at Km100 of Jalan Kuantan-Segamat near Politeknik Muadzam Shah at 10.10pm yesterday.
Rompin police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the crash involved a convoy of 17 motorcycles travelling from Gemas, Negri Sembilan, to Kuala Terengganu.
He said one rider lost control and fell onto the road before being hit by another motorcycle in the convoy, causing both motorcycles to catch fire.
The injured riders, identified as Mohd Redwan Maamur, 41, and Safiuddin Mohd Arshad, 34, are receiving treatment at Hospital Muadzam Shah.
The two-day RXZ Members 8.0 motorcycle gathering begins today at the Gong Badak Motor Racing Circuit in Kuala Nerus, Terengganu.

Title: Malaysia's AI push drives growth, opens doors in UAE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming central to economic growth, productivity and competitiveness, industry insiders said.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo has said that AI is set to become a major driver of Malaysia's economic growth, with the technology expected to contribute between RM13 billion and RM20 billion annually to gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030.
Malaysia's AI policies, including the National AI Roadmap, position AI as a cross-sector technology to accelerate digital transformation across industries and the public sector.
"AI adoption is expanding across manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, retail, logistics, agriculture and government services, supported by growing investments in cloud computing and data centre infrastructure.
"Malaysia is building up on AI across all sectors. In fact, there are a few companies which have invested in AI technology now heading to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to seek opportunities," an industry insider told Business Times.
The UAE has emerged as one of the region's fastest-growing AI markets. Consultancy PwC estimates AI could contribute nearly US$96 billion to the UAE economy by 2030, equivalent to about 13.6 per cent of the country's GDP.
Reflecting that trend, Nasdaq-listed Robo.ai Inc. recently announced a joint venture with Abu Dhabi-based Eleven International Holdings to establish Alif Holding, an AI-focused industrial technology company.
Alif Holding will develop intelligent software and smart equipment for government, infrastructure and industrial customers across the UAE, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and international markets.
"Alif Holding is designed as a full-stack AI industrial group," said Benjamin Zhai, chief executive officer of Robo.ai.
"Governments, critical infrastructure operators and industry across this region are investing in AI at national scale, and they need partners able to deliver complete systems end to end," he said in a statement.
The venture will focus on government- and public-sector projects as well as mission-critical industries, including energy, oil and gas, ports, public safety, utilities, mining, transportation, smart cities and critical infrastructure.
It also plans to establish engineering, assembly and manufacturing capabilities in Abu Dhabi. The group's development strategy includes acquiring proven technologies, integrating them into a unified platform, manufacturing in the UAE to international standards and expanding into regional and global markets.
Robo.ai said Alif Holding will adopt a technology-neutral, open-architecture approach by partnering with international providers of AI, robotics, sensors, software, communications, and public safety and security technologies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Private sector credit growth holds steady in June
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's credit growth remained resilient in June while banks continued to maintain strong liquidity and asset quality, even as inflation eased further, according to Bank Negara Malaysia's latest monthly highlights.
Credit to the private non-financial sector expanded 6.4 per cent in June, supported by sustained growth in both outstanding loans, which increased 6.0 per cent, and corporate bonds, which rose 8.1 per cent.
Business loan growth strengthened to 7.2 per cent from 7.0 per cent in May, driven mainly by lending to non-small and medium enterprises, particularly for working capital.
Outstanding household loans grew 5.3 per cent, slightly slower than the 5.5 per cent recorded in May, amid moderating growth in personal use loans.
Bank Negara said the banking sector's asset quality remained sound, with gross and net impaired loan ratios broadly unchanged at 1.4 per cent and 1.0 per cent, respectively.
The loan loss coverage ratio, including regulatory reserves, remained prudent at 124.6 per cent of gross impaired loans, compared with 124.1 per cent in May.
Banks also maintained ample liquidity buffers, with the aggregate Liquidity Coverage Ratio improving to 149.7 per cent from 149.2 per cent, ensuring resilience against potential liquidity shocks.
Meanwhile, headline inflation and core inflation both moderated to 1.9 per cent in June from 2.0 per cent in May, reflecting easing external cost pressures and slower price increases across several core items.
Bank Negara said the moderation in headline inflation was mainly due to lower retail fuel inflation, particularly for RON97 petrol and diesel.
Lower core inflation, meanwhile, reflected base effects from higher streaming services inflation recorded in June last year, as well as slower price increases for jewellery and watches amid softer global gold prices.
Economic activity showed mixed trends, with the Index of Wholesale and Retail Trade growth slowing to 3.1 per cent in May from 6.2 per cent in April.
Retail trade growth, however, improved to 4.4 per cent from 3.9 per cent, driven mainly by stronger sales at non-specialised stores and higher automotive fuel sales at specialised retailers.
This was offset by slower wholesale trade growth and weaker motor vehicle sales, particularly in other specialised wholesale activities, wholesale of household goods and motor vehicle sales.
On the financial markets, Bank Negara said global developments continued to be shaped by evolving expectations for the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) policy rate path.
Markets increasingly priced in the possibility of a US interest rate hike by the end of 2026, supported by stronger-than-expected labour market data, elevated inflation and the Fed's updated economic projections.
Against this backdrop, the ringgit depreciated 2.6 per cent against the US dollar in June as the greenback strengthened globally.
The yield on the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose four basis points amid higher net bond issuances, while the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI fell 1.1 per cent, weighed down by non-resident outflows.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: USM appoints Noor Hazlina as deputy vice-chancellor
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has appointed Professor Datin Dr Noor Hazlina Ahmad as its new deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International), effective Aug 3.
She succeeds Professor Datuk Dr Narimah Samat, who has completed her term in the position.
Noor Hazlina, an academic specialising in entrepreneurship, innovation, leadership and organisational development, holds a PhD in Entrepreneurship from the University of Adelaide, a Master of Business Administration from USM and a Bachelor of Science in Humanities (Psychology) from the International Islamic University Malaysia.
Before her appointment, she served as dean of the USM School of Management since 2019, where she led strategic initiatives to strengthen academic excellence, internationalisation and institutional sustainability.
During her tenure, the school introduced several programmes, including the Master of Business Analytics in collaboration with the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) and the Master of Professional Management with the Malaysian Bar Council.
She also spearheaded a 2022 collaboration with Egypt's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology to develop digital leadership talent among top Egyptian students, further expanding USM's international footprint.
Noor Hazlina has also driven flexible learning initiatives, including offshore programmes, Open and Distance Learning (ODL), micro-credentials and stackable degree pathways.
Among her key initiatives were the development of a micro-credential-based Bachelor of Management (Honours) programme with QSR Brands and the exploration of an AI-guided Master of Management programme.
She is currently president of the Asian Academy of Management for the 2025-2027 term and chairs the Strategic Investment in Education Working Group under the National Education Reform Study led by the Academy of Sciences Malaysia.
USM said her appointment would strengthen the university's academic and internationalisation agenda through educational innovation, expanded global partnerships, improved graduate employability and efforts to reinforce its position as a leading global institution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citadel buys most of Situational's stock holdings after AI share rout, sources say
Article:
NEW YORK: Situational Awareness, an AI-focused hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold the bulk of its stock portfolio to Ken Griffin's Citadel after being battered by heavy losses in its tech holdings, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.
Situational was forced to unwind most of its public equities portfolio, which included sizable holdings in several prominent AI names that have been rocked by the recent market selloff, the sources said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are confidential.
The fund was under pressure to either raise fresh capital from investors or offload its entire book, and eventually chose the latter option, the sources added. Situational held positions in several prominent tech names including Broadcom, Intel, and CoreWeave, according to its most recent regulatory filings.
Since the fund's launch in 2024, Aschenbrenner has garnered a cult-like following among investors for his prescient bets on the AI sector that propelled his fund to a lofty 439 per cent return from the start of the year until the end of June.
The fund was down around 67 per cent so far in July after incurring heavy losses on AI stocks, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing a source who saw a letter the firm sent to investors.
Aschenbrenner blamed short sellers who targeted the firm's positions for exacerbating losses, the report said.
The firm did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment outside business hours.
A number of top Wall Street prime brokers, including Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Citigroup, helped facilitate the deal between Citadel and Aschenbrenner's fund, the sources told Reuters.
Griffin's Citadel, which has about US$71 billion of assets under management, is one of the world's most profitable and largest hedge funds.
As part of the deal, Citadel is picking up the portion of Situational's public portfolio that was financed by leverage from brokers, the sources said. They said Situational will hold a book of roughly US$10 billion after the deal comprised of stocks as well as private investments in companies like Anthropic. Situational has not sold its stake in Anthropic, the sources said.
AI MELTDOWN
Global hedge funds are grappling with their biggest monthly drawdown on record as AI stocks have been routed across the board, erasing much of the gains from crowded bets in the sector. Asia-focused fundamental long-short funds are down 18.6 per cent on average this month through July 28, Goldman Sachs said in a prime brokerage note sent to clients this week.
Stock-picking hedge funds have been rushing to unwind their positions in AI names, as they covered short positions and sold long positions in relatively equal amounts, according to a note from Morgan Stanley's prime brokerage unit sent to clients on Wednesday.
Hedge funds typically take on large amounts of leverage from lenders to take bigger swings at the markets in order to amplify their returns. However, such leveraged bets can backfire when the markets move against positions taken by funds, forcing margin calls from prime brokers. That can result in a vicious cycle, where the margin calls trigger sales, extending market downturns that beget more selling.
It is not clear whether Aschenbrenner's fund faced margin calls from its lenders before striking the deal with Citadel. The hedge fund, which earlier managed about US$20 billion of assets and currently has about 20 employees, has used leverage to boost its positions in the past - much like its peers.
Aschenbrenner's success attracted big-name backers like secretive trading giant Jane Street. Other investors include Stripe co-founders Patrick and John Collison, as well as Meta Platforms executives Daniel Gross and Nat Friedman.
The Wall Street Journal reported the deal between Citadel and Situational earlier on Thursday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Syerleena condemns dog's killing, calls for transparent probe
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Bendera member of parliament Syerleena Abdul Rashid has condemned the killing of a dog known as Rocky and called for a swift, transparent and independent investigation into the incident.
Syerleena said in a statement today that the brutal killing of Rocky, described as a pet and a beloved companion, had shocked Malaysians and left a grieving family mourning the loss of a cherished animal.
"As a Malay Muslim, I reject without hesitation the brutal killing of Rocky," she said.
It was reported that the dog died during a capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, after Majlis Bandaraya Diraja Klang personnel released the loop equipment being used following an incident involving members of the public.
The operation, carried out from 8.30pm to midnight on July 29, followed official
complaints
from residents over safety concerns linked to an increase in stray dogs in the area.
Syerleena said there was "nothing Islamic about cruelty" and rejected attempts to justify violence against animals on religious grounds.
She said Islam teaches rahmah (mercy), compassion and justice, adding that even when dealing with animals that may pose a risk, they should be treated with restraint rather than brutality.
The lawmaker also expressed concern over reports that Rocky's family was allegedly met with indifference when seeking help and was told the dog did not have a licence.
"If those reports are true, that is unacceptable. Whether or not a pet is licensed is not an excuse for brutality, nor should it diminish the seriousness of a violent act," she said.
She said that any administrative issues should be addressed through due process and could never justify cruelty.
Syerleena said any breach of the law should be investigated by the relevant authorities, adding that no one has the right to take the law into their own hands.
"Those who take the law into their own hands are not upholding justice — they are undermining it," she said.
She called for a swift, transparent and independent investigation into the incident, saying those responsible must be held fully accountable if wrongdoing was established.
"Justice for Rocky is not just about one dog. It is about defending the rule of law, protecting the vulnerable and making it unequivocally clear that vigilantism has no place in Malaysia," she said.
